advisories.title: The allowlist refusal is recorded per class, while G07 v3's gate-level filesystem standing — UNPOPULATED, matrix INCOMPLETE, a separate later act required — is not carried
advisories.detail: The subject records filesystemAllowlistPopulated false on each of the four classes and refuses to populate an allowlist five more times. That is accurate and it satisfies the dispatch. But G07 v3 treats the filesystem question as one gate-level fact rather than a per-class one: its filesystems block carries standing UNPOPULATED, a remainingObligation that 'the G07 supported-filesystem coverage-domain set … exists in no live governing source in this corpus', matrixStanding INCOMPLETE on the filesystem axis until a later act supplies the set, and a laterAct clause stating that act is a different artifact, is not a leftover-join, and is not leftover-design closed there. None of that reaches the catalog. The corpus independently treats this as live: DR-126's OBL-G07-BOUNDARY exists partly to say G07's supported-filesystems coverage domain is a different question that DR-126 does not own.
advisories.whyItStaysAdvisory: The catalog's stated scope is the four named corpus classes, and within that scope it is exact. It claims nothing about matrix completeness, so no reader is misled into thinking the filesystem axis is settled — the four false flags and the refusals all point the other way. Nothing here is wrong; a neighbouring fact is simply absent, and the artifact never undertook to carry it.
advisories.residue: A reader holding only this catalog learns that no allowlist is populated here, but not that the gate's matrix is incomplete on that axis pending a separate, unowned act. Since this artifact exists to continue G07 leftover-design, that is the one piece of context it would most usefully carry. A single clause quoting the UNPOPULATED standing and the matrixStanding INCOMPLETE would close it, without populating anything.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 1 advisory. Twenty attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject df72a0d9 at 0444, 4477 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; DR-G07 and DR-103 both OPEN and untouched; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All four cited digests reproduce, and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head. The dispatch's equality attack fails against the artifact: namedCorpusNotAuthored equals live G07 v3 exactly as an ordered list — hostile archive, hostile path, hostile loader, TOCTOU — and the four classes' memberVerbatim values in order equal that same list, so the class array is a faithful expansion rather than a re-wording. I checked why this catalog is thinner than the G16 one I reviewed before it, since missing exactByteIntent and passProperty could look like truncation: G07 v3 has no namedCorpusClasses key at all, so four member strings are the entire quotable surface and the catalog carries all of it. The filesystem allowlist is unpopulated at every site, verified by field path rather than keyword count — there is no filesystems key, no path, glob or filesystem identifier anywhere, five refusals and four per-class false flags — and G07 v3's own filesystems block is not copied, partially copied or guessed at. All seven 64-hex strings in the artifact were enumerated by path and all seven are the four pins, so no authored digest or treeRootDigest value hides among them. The one claim that a search appears to falsify took source reading to settle, and I record the path because the search alone would have produced a false finding. The subject asserts that no leftover-join exists for this gate; searching every leftover-join in the corpus returns platform-tcb-leftover-join v1 and v2, both naming DR-G07 and both carrying an obligation called OBL-G07-BOUNDARY. Neither is a leftover-join for this gate: both sit on registerRow DR-126, and OBL-G07-BOUNDARY is a boundary marker at leftoverDesign false with rideStanding rides-G07 whose entire content disclaims G07 territory, recording that DR-126 does not re-own archive extraction, symlink or TOCTOU and that G07's supported-filesystems coverage domain is a different question it does not own. It is absent from DR-126's own leftoverDesign summary. The claim is accurate. I also checked the registerRow, which is DR-G07 here where the sibling G16 catalog used the substantive row DR-121; the divergence is explained rather than careless, since that catalog continues an obligation carried by a DR-121 leftover-join while here no join exists and OBL-G07-HARNESS-SPEC lives on the gate row in G07 v3's own whatThisCloses. One advisory, not barring acceptance: the allowlist refusal is recorded per class, but G07 v3's gate-level filesystem standing — UNPOPULATED, matrixStanding INCOMPLETE on that axis, and a separate later act required that no one yet owns — is not carried. Nothing is misrepresented and the catalog's scope is the corpus classes, so this stays advisory; the residue is that a reader holding only this file learns no allowlist is populated here but not that the gate's matrix is incomplete pending an unowned act, which for an artifact continuing G07 leftover-design is the context most worth having. Separately and deliberately not raised as a numbered advisory: the DR-G07 register row also reads 'not authored' while G07 v3 exists. That is now the fifth row in the same condition after DR-G09, DR-G15, DR-G26 and DR-G16, this subject asserts no authoring close, and I recommended in the preceding verdict that the coordinator dispose of the family in one act; repeating it as a fifth advisory would inflate the count without adding information. One disclosure: I reviewed this harness's v1 and v2 earlier in this session and rejected both, one under the same do-not-invent-a-filesystem-allowlist constraint, so I came to this catalog already holding a view of G07's open items — which is why advisory A1 was easy for me to see and would be harder for a reviewer without that history.
